- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase early forecast values, especially if recent history shows downward trend.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment — cap forecast overshoots at 2x recent high or 1.5x prior peak.
- If sentiment history shows strong reversal (e.g., from negative to positive), model often fails to adjust — apply mean reversion bias: reduce forecast by 15–30% of prior peak if sentiment flips upward.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate in high-sentiment periods and underestimate in low-sentiment; apply sentiment-weighted smoothing: forecast = 0.7×prior + 0.3×sentiment-adjusted trend.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and history shows mean-reverting behavior, model often fails to correct — apply 10–20% downward adjustment to forecast if recent 3–5 days show no clear trend.
